newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA MAY CPI BACKS RATE CUT HOPES - ECONOMISTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA MAY CPI BACKS RATE CUT HOPES - ECONOMISTS.

text.p: South African economists and bond dealers cheered Tuesday's weaker-than-expected May Consumer Price Index figures as reinforcing the argument that official interest rates could fall around September.
"It was better than expected and I think it confirms that we saw the peak in April and we would look for it to continue to trend downwards," said Rand Merchant Bank Treasury economist Julia Roy.
"We're looking for a (one percent) rate cut in the third quarter -- August-September -- and it helps to strengthen that view," she added.
South Africa's all-items consumer price index rose 0.3 percent in May from April after rising 0.9 percent in April, the Central Statistical Service said.
The year-on-year rise was 9.5 percent versus April's 9.9 percent.
A Reuters consensus poll of economists forecast a 0.6 percent month-on-month increase and a 9.8 percent year-on-year rise.

Economists warned, however, the South African Reserve Bank was likely hold off on adjustments to monetary policy until it had a chance to assess the affect of the lifting of exchange controls on individuals from July 1.
"The CPI figure is positive (for an interest rate cut) but nothing's going to happen until the dust has settled from July 1," said Tony Twine, economist at Econometrix.
South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel is due to announce the foreign exchange caps for individuals at 1400 GMT on Wednesday.
Food inflation hit its highest level since October 1996, at an annual rate of 11.7 percent but economists were generally unfased by this.
"The food inflation rate was comparatively low this time a year ago, it's come from that base," said one.

The food figures were boosted by a 1.8 percent rise from April in milk, cheese and eggs, a 1.6 percent rise in sugar prices and a 1.3 percent rise in both the vegetables and the fish and other seafood categories.
Economists said May's data was an apparent confirmation of wider expectations that CPI had peaked in April and an endorsement of Reserve Bank monetary policy to date.

"9.5 pct for May might indicate that we're out of the woods. Economists had for a long time been calling April as the turning point and this is at least an indicator that they might have been right," said Econometrix's Twine.
"It does indicate a turning point in the CPI and I think also lower-than-expected CPI indicates successful implementation of Stals' policy," said ABN Amro corporate dealer Craig Ferreira.
South Africa's Bank rate stands at 17.0 pct and was last hiked by one percentage point on November 21 last year.
The bullish CPI data had no impact on bonds amid talk that the figure was leaked before 0900 GMT official release.
The R150 was last at 14.495 pct off a day's strongest level of 14.465 pct reached before May CPI data released.
